title: Product-based kinetic analysis reveals limitations of substrate depletion method for assessing bile salt hydrolase activity
desc: Bacterial bile salt hydrolases (BSH) catalyze the initial step in microbial bile acid transformation and play a key role in host-microbiome interactions. However, reliable ex vivo assessment of BSH activity, particularly its kinetic characterization, remains limited. Here, we developed an LC–MS-based assay to characterize BSH activity in murine cecal content and evaluated its performance in a model of cholestasis induced by 3,5-diethoxycarbonyl-1,4-dihydrocollidine (DDC). Enzymatic activity was assessed using three major tauro-conjugated substrates: taurocholic (TCA), taurochenodeoxycholic (TCDCA), and taurodeoxycholic acid (TDCA). Product-based analysis revealed Michaelis–Menten-type kinetics for all substrates. Apparent Km values increased in the order TDCA < TCDCA < TCA, indicating decreasing substrate affinity, while maximal reaction rates followed the reverse trend (TCA < TCDCA < TDCA). In DDC-treated mice, BSH activity was reduced, as reflected by decreased apparent Vmax. In contrast, measurements performed at sub-Km concentrations were variable and did not consistently reflect the expected group-level differences. Similarly, substrate depletion approaches failed to distinguish between experimental groups. Among the tested substrates, TCDCA provided the most robust readout due to minimal endogenous background and clear differences at near-saturating concentrations. These findings highlight the importance of Vmax-oriented analysis and multi-concentration assessment for reliable evaluation of BSH activity.
